newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sacks nine police officers.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sacks nine police officers.

text.p: The Philippine national police chief has sacked a provincial commander and eight senior officers over the proliferation of illegal gambling in a province near Manila, police said on Sunday.
This brought to 13 the number of senior officers relieved of their commands in the past week for failing to stop an illegal numbers game called "jueteng" in their areas.
Police Director-General Recaredo Sarmiento ordered the dismissal of the nine officers after anti-vice squads raided gambling places in Rizal province.
Jueteng is a lottery-type game which involves picking a combination of numbers from one to 37 and is popular around the country because bets can be as low as five pesos (US19 cents).
President Fidel Ramos ordered a crackdown on jueteng operators after newspapers alleged some local officials were receiving bribes in exchange for allowing the game to continue.
Police say jueteng operators collect up to 60 million pesos ($2.3 million) every day in bets and pay a third of the amount, or 18 million pesos ($690,000), to officials as bribes.
